key_findings: Ablation of spinal inhibitory Kcnip2GlyT2 interneurons selectively increased cold sensitivity and cold aversion, while their chemogenetic activation reduced cold and heat sensitivity.
Kcnip2GlyT2 neurons are preferentially activated by cold, receive TRPM8 (icilin-sensitive) input, and produce bicuculline/strychnine-sensitive IPSCs in lamina I spinoparabrachial output neurons.
